function.name: EventSettingsApi_create_website_alert_config
function.description: Creates a configuration for website alerting within the system, allowing users to define conditions under which alerts should be triggered for a website. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The name for the website alert configuration.

description.description: A detailed description for the website alert configuration.

severity.description: The severity level of the alert when triggered.

triggering.description: Flag indicating whether the alert configuration should also trigger an incident.

websiteId.description: The unique identifier of the website for which the alert configuration is created.

tagFilterExpression.description: A boolean expression used to filter the scope of website beacons based on tags.

granularity.description: The evaluation granularity in seconds used for detection of threshold violations.

rule.description: The type of rule this alert configuration pertains to, such as 'traffic spike' or 'downtime'.

threshold.description: The threshold value that, when exceeded, will trigger the alert. This is a float type value.

timeThreshold.description: The time duration in seconds during which the threshold must be exceeded to trigger the alert.

alertChannelIds.description: A list of alert channel IDs defined in Instana to which the alert notifications will be sent.

message.content:
**Short answer:**  
Instana’s public REST‑API isn’t exposed with a “major.minor” version prefix – all calls hit the same base path (`…/instana/api/*`). Underneath, Instana keeps track of its software build (e.g., “5.x.y”) and exposes that information in the **Health & Version** page of the web console or via the `X‑Instana‑Version` response header, but client code never needs to hard‑code a numeric API version.

---

### Why Instana doesn’t publish a separate API version

| Reason | What it means for developers |
|--------|------------------------------|
| **Backward‑compatibility guarantee** | Every change to the API is made *backwards‑compatible*. Existing integrations continue working without modification. |
| **Simplified SDKs** | Libraries don’t have to switch between multiple endpoint sets; they just target the one set of URLs. |
| **Rapid iteration** | New features can be added behind feature flags or optional parameters without breaking existing consumers. |

> **Bottom line:** Treat the Instana API as a *single* contract. When a new Instana platform release ships, the API stays the same unless a breaking change is explicitly announced—then it comes with a deprecation window.

---

### How to discover what backend Instana version you’re talking to

If you really need to know the exact Instana build running on your cluster:

```http
GET https://{your-instana-host}/instana/api/status
```

Response snippet:

```json
{
  "build": {
    "version": "5.12.7",
    "commitHash": "a1b2c3d"
  },
  ...
}
```

Alternatively, inspect the HTTP headers returned by any API request:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
...
X-Instana-Version: 5.12.7
```

These values let you correlate behavior against known bug fixes or feature rollouts documented in the [Release Notes](https://www.instana.com/docs/release-notes).

---

### Quick reference for common endpoints

| Endpoint | Purpose | Example |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `/services` | List services monitored by Instana | `GET https://.../instana/api/services` |
| `/metrics/{serviceName}` | Retrieve metrics for a service | `GET .../instana/api/metrics/my-service` |
| `/alerts` | Manage alert configurations | `POST .../instana/api/alerts` |
| `/configurations/events` | Create event‑based alert configs (see below) | `POST .../instana/api/configurations/events` |

All paths share the same base (`/instana/api`) regardless of the Instana product edition (Cloud vs On‑Prem). No `/v1`, `/v2`, … prefixes appear.

---

#### TL;DR

- **No external API version number** – the interface remains constant across Instana releases.
- To learn the actual Instana build, query `/status` or read the `X-Instana-Version` header.
- Keep your integration simple: point to `<base-url>/instana/api/<resource>` and trust Instana’s backward‑compatibility guarantees.

Feel free to ping us if you run into a scenario where you think a particular field disappeared or changed unexpectedly—we’ll confirm whether it was intentional or a regression!
